label: From Flow to Inequality
notes: This chapter, printed pages 719 through 730, closes the gradient-flow arc by harvesting functional inequalities from the entropy flow. The plan is to read every inequality as a quantitative decay statement: how fast Boltzmann entropy falls along heat flow, and which curvature lower bound certifies that rate.

label: Entropy as the Driving Functional
notes: We fix the Boltzmann entropy relative to a reference measure as the energy that the flow minimizes. Its Wasserstein gradient flow is exactly the Fokker-Planck or heat equation, so the abstract machinery from the previous chapters now drives a concrete diffusion whose decay we can quantify.

label: Entropy Dissipation Equals Fisher Information
notes: The key bookkeeping identity says the time derivative of entropy along the flow is minus the Fisher information. Dissipation is therefore not abstract: it is a computable integral of the squared gradient of the log-density, the quantity that the lab shades as an inequality gap.

label: Three Quantities: H, W, I
notes: Three measurements organize the chapter: relative entropy H measuring disorder, Wasserstein distance W measuring transport cost to equilibrium, and Fisher information I measuring instantaneous dissipation. The HWI inequality binds all three into one triangle, and every classical inequality is a face of it.

label: The HWI Inequality
notes: The HWI inequality bounds the entropy gap by a product of Wasserstein distance and the square root of Fisher information, corrected by a curvature term. Proved by Otto and Villani, it interpolates along the displacement geodesic between the current density and equilibrium, reading convexity off the second derivative.

label: Displacement Convexity Supplies Curvature
notes: The curvature constant K enters through displacement convexity of the entropy along Wasserstein geodesics. A lower Ricci bound makes entropy K-convex, so the interpolation argument keeps a quadratic remainder of the right sign. Without this convexity the HWI estimate loses its teeth.

label: Log-Sobolev from HWI
notes: Setting the target to equilibrium and using Young's inequality on the HWI product collapses the W term, leaving entropy bounded by Fisher information over twice K. That is the logarithmic Sobolev inequality, the exact statement that entropy decays exponentially at rate two K along the flow.

label: Talagrand from HWI
notes: Dropping the nonnegative Fisher term at equilibrium turns HWI into Talagrand's transport inequality: the squared Wasserstein distance to equilibrium is controlled by twice the entropy over K. Thus a single curvature bound delivers both concentration of measure and the spectral-gap-style decay simultaneously.

label: Exponential Decay of Entropy
notes: Combining the dissipation identity with the log-Sobolev inequality gives a Gronwall differential inequality for entropy. Its solution is exponential decay at rate two K, so the density relaxes to equilibrium geometrically. The Wasserstein distance inherits the same exponential rate through Talagrand.

label: The Otto-Villani Theorem
notes: Otto and Villani's theorem packages the logic: under a curvature-dimension lower bound, log-Sobolev implies Talagrand, and HWI implies both. The Riemannian geometry of Wasserstein space, not ad hoc analysis, is what makes these implications transparent and dimension-free in the right coordinates.

label: Computational Footprint
notes: The notebook makes the chain inspectable: it samples entropy and Fisher-information proxies along a discretized flow and shades the inequality gap. The invariant check asserts that the sampled dissipation gap stays nonnegative, the numerical signature that the HWI estimate has not been violated.

label: Recap and Outlook
notes: We turned the entropy gradient flow into a generator of functional inequalities. The HWI triangle unifies log-Sobolev and Talagrand through displacement convexity. The next steps extend these tools to spaces with only synthetic Ricci bounds, where the same transport arguments survive without smoothness.
